findings_detail.description: On a Staging1 connection, the first non-banner packet of ANY opcode, read in clear, now arms the cipher, sends SMSG_RESUME_COMMS and promotes the socket to the session's stream 1. Nothing checks that the opcode is CMSG_AUTH_CONTINUED_SESSION, the payload digest is not verified, and m_bannerDone is no longer consulted. If the opcode is anything else, it falls through to m_gateway.Deliver(m_session, ...) because the ticket already set m_session. Before this PR the cipher was armed after the banner, so the first framed packet had to be enciphered with the session key, which was an implicit proof of possession. Now a peer that only shares the victim's source address (NAT, shared host) and wins the race to the stream-1 port can take over the second stream and inject one arbitrary plaintext game opcode into the authenticated session without knowing the session key.
findings_detail.fix_sketch: In the Staging1 branch, return false unless opcode == CMSG_AUTH_CONTINUED_SESSION with a 36-byte payload; carry the account name on RedirectTicket and verify the SHA-1(account || K || seed) digest before arming, sending RESUME_COMMS or promoting.

findings_detail.description: SendResumeComms() runs before PromoteToSlotOne() has checked that the session still exists and that this socket's redirect generation is current. When PromoteToSlotOne() fails (session gone or superseded redirect), the client has already been told to adopt this stale socket as stream 1. Per the comment in SendResumeComms, that makes it retire whatever held the slot, which may be the newer valid stream, and the server then closes this socket.
findings_detail.fix_sketch: Check links liveness and generation before sending SMSG_RESUME_COMMS, e.g. split AttachSlotOne into a validate/reserve step, then send RESUME_COMMS, then flush the held queue.

findings_detail.description: The startup path (`initialize == true`) now derives the next reset from `m_gameTime` instead of `time(NULL)`. The sibling init routines in this file deliberately use `time(NULL)`, with the comment "game time not yet init" (line 1803). findings_detail.description: The extracted `NextMonthlyQuestReset` keeps `tm_isdst` from `now` when it calls `mktime` for the first of next month. This is carried over from the old code, but the new World.h comment promises "local midnight" and the PR's goal is a single firing. When DST ends before the next 1st, the result is 23:00 on the last day of the month, so the reset fires then and again an hour later at real midnight. When DST starts, the reset lands at 01:00. The new test rows do not span a DST change, so they do not catch this.
findings_detail.fix_sketch: Set `localTm.tm_isdst = -1;` before `mktime(&localTm)` and add a test row whose month spans a DST transition.

findings_detail.description: `EmitCase(RandomBits(...), RandomBits(64), BigNumber(d))` draws from the shared `rng` in several arguments of one call, and C++ leaves argument evaluation order unspecified. Compilers that evaluate left-to-right and right-to-left will hand different values to a/b/n, so the generated table depends on the compiler despite the 'fixed seed: the table is reproducible' claim. Regenerating CryptoGoldenVectors.h on another toolchain rewrites every big-integer case. The same pattern recurs at lines 207, 210, 215, 227, 238, 243, 253, 261 and 268.
findings_detail.fix_sketch: Draw each random operand into a named local in a fixed order (`BigNumber a = RandomBits(..); BigNumber b = RandomBits(..);`) before calling EmitCase.

findings_detail.description: `Hex()` builds a std::string from `v.AsHexStr()` and never frees the returned buffer. AuthSocket.cpp and the capture tool's `HexOf` both release it with `OPENSSL_free`, so the caller owns it. Every CHECK_STR in Replay leaks, and the identical helper at CryptoGoldenTest.cpp line 30 leaks about ten buffers per big-integer case (up to 4096-bit values), which would trip LeakSanitizer.
findings_detail.fix_sketch: Copy the `HexOf(BigNumber&)` pattern from the capture tool: keep the pointer, build the string, `OPENSSL_free` it, then return.

findings_detail.description: The SRP_*_WIDTH constants in the anonymous namespace now duplicate `Srp6::EphemeralWidth`, `SessionKeyWidth`, `GeneratorWidth` and `ReconnectWidth`. findings_detail.fix_sketch: Delete the local constants and use the `Srp6::` widths in AuthSocket.cpp, or at least static_assert that they are equal, including `s_BYTE_SIZE == Srp6::SaltWidth`.
